findings.english_quote: “For” corresponds to bracketed [pro], supplied in the working edition from the reported pseudo-Cyprian De aleatoribus 2 quotation and absent from the cited Vulgata manuscripts. The quotation is an indirect witness; no fresh collation of its manuscripts is claimed.
findings.issue: The quotation locator conflicts with the supplied attributed apparatus transcription, which reports “ps-Cypr. de Aleat. 3,” not section 2. The note correctly identifies [pro] as an editorial supplement and does not claim fresh manuscript verification, but its specific citation is not supported by the supplied report.
findings.suggested_revision: Cite De aleatoribus 3 as the locator reported by the supplied apparatus transcription, or provide evidence explaining a numbering convention under which section 2 is the corresponding location. Retain the distinction between editorial supply and manuscript text.

findings.source_quote: quodsi ipsi pastores dissipati reperti fuerint, quid respondebunt [pro] pecoribus his?
findings.english_quote: If the shepherds themselves are ruined, what answer will they give for this flock?[c]
findings.issue: The simplified edition omits reperti, “found.” The source frames the shepherds’ condition as something discovered in the assessment, continuing the preceding repeated language of finding the flock healthy or ruined. Merely being ruined does not fully preserve that assessment wording.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction for fresh review: “If the shepherds themselves are found ruined, what answer will they give for this flock?[c]”

findings.suggested_revision: Use the reported section 3 locator, or supply evidence documenting why section 2 is an equivalent citation under another numbering convention. Continue identifying [pro] as editorial supply rather than preserved wording in the cited Vulgata manuscripts.

summary: Both editions require limited revision. Apart from the findings listed, clause-by-clause review supports their fidelity to the selected Latin working text, including its necessity, negations, innocent-kind restriction, repentance terminology, speaker attribution, and demanding assertions about shepherds. The disclosed collective one-spirit rendering and lexical alternatives do not require replacing the working reading. This review evaluates supplied text and attributed reports; it does not authenticate unseen editions, manuscript handwriting, or exhaustive collation.
